facts: Deed plans are an essential element of buying and selling land, and the title plan cannot describe land more accurately than the pre-registration deeds permit.
Any plan lodged with a registration application or search must allow the land to be identified clearly on the Ordnance Survey map.
A plan supporting an official search and later deed must show the precise extent, a stated scale, a north point and enough surrounding detail, and must not be marked for identification purposes only.
Practice guide 40 supplement 3 was updated on 1 June 2026 and applies to England and Wales.
The guide distinguishes an exact, invisible legal boundary from a visible physical feature such as a fence, wall or hedge.
Most registered titles show general boundaries, and no standard tolerance, measurement or ratio defines the relationship between a title-plan line and the legal boundary.
A determined boundary records the exact line of a registered-estate boundary rather than merely its general position.
Before proceeding, the registrar must be satisfied that the exact line is identified, an arguable case is shown and adjoining owners can be identified and notified.
A determined-boundary plan should clearly identify start, end and turning points, show surrounding detail and orientation, and preferably use a scale no smaller than 1:200.
Practice guide 40 supplement 5 was updated on 13 July 2026.
A registered title consists of the register, the title plan and any documents referred to in the register and filed at HM Land Registry.
The title plan graphically identifies the general extent and may also reference easements, covenants or land removed from the title.
Practice guide 41 supplement 5 sets technical plan requirements for estate-boundary approval and estate-plan approval.
Plans must show scale and orientation, be based on an accurate survey and show measurements in metric form; 1:500 is preferred where detail remains clear.
Plans marked for identification only, do not scale, or carrying reliability disclaimers are not acceptable.
The developing-estate registration services use simple documentation and do not charge fees for the approval services.
HM Land Registry states that straightforward approvals will be given within five working days and applicants will be contacted within five days if problems arise.
Developing-estate plans should show scale and orientation, use an accurate land survey, use metric measurements and clearly define and number each plot.
The live Design code area dataset reports 11 geographical areas.
The dataset reports six data providers.
Its origin is MHCLG-created interim data that is intended to be replaced when authoritative sources become available.
The Design code area type dataset contains 10 area types.
References include high-rise-city, town-city-centre, industrial-areas, villages and rural-settlements.
The Design code rule category dataset reports 78 categories.
Category references include heritage-assets, street-network, public-transport, walking, cycling and services-utilities.
The live Locally listed building dataset reports 448 records.
It is described as an experimental dataset assembled from data.gov.uk while a formal local-list specification is developed with authorities.
The Local Planning Authority dataset reports 337 administrative boundaries.
It supports identifying the authority responsible for a planning application and uses Office for National Statistics and Ordnance Survey boundary data.
The live Local plan dataset reports 1,050 plans.
Separate rows represent current, emerging or historical plans and can be used to assess plan dates, housing intentions and application or investment context.
The live plan timetable dataset reports 8,927 timetable records.
The dataset describes plan-preparation stages and expected milestones for authorities.
The Planning application dataset reports 100,627 applications.
The current dataset is MHCLG-created interim data rather than a complete mandatory national submission.
The Development plan document dataset reports 2,686 documents.
Each row links to a published authority document and can be combined with the document-type dataset to locate items such as transport assessments.
The Development plan document type dataset contains 16 types.
References include local-plan, area-action-plan, policies-map, strategic-flood-risk-assessment, core-strategy and site-allocations.

Its origin is MHCLG-created interim data intended for replacement by authoritative sources.
The Flood risk type dataset contains five types.
The dataset reports one provider and authoritative-source origin.
The references are fluvial-model, tidal-model, fluvial-event, tidal-event and coastal-event.
The Flood risk level dataset contains three levels.
The dataset reports one provider and authoritative-source origin.
The live Conservation area dataset reports 11,008 areas.
The dataset reports 160 providers and a collector run on 31 July 2026.
The service warns that the dataset remains incomplete and contains duplicate conservation areas that are being reconciled.
The Local green space dataset currently reports zero records.
It currently reports zero providers and no collector attempt.
The dataset page nevertheless exposes CSV, JSON, GeoJSON and Parquet download routes.
The live Local plan boundary dataset reports 364 boundaries.
The boundary identifies the area covered by a local plan so users can understand which plan applies to a site.
The Local plan document dataset currently reports zero records.

The Environment Agency 1 metre DTM is a raster terrain model covering approximately 99 percent of England.
It is produced from last or only laser returns with surface objects removed using algorithms and manual editing.
The dataset uses EPSG:27700 and combines surveys from 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022.
The 2 metre DTM covers approximately 99 percent of England at 2 metre resolution.
The 2022 composite combines time-stamped and National LIDAR Programme surveys and prefers the newest best-resolution coverage.
Its metadata records creation on 8 February 2023 and revision on 15 December 2023.
The 10 metre DTM covers approximately 99 percent of England.
It is resampled from the 2 metre DTM using bilinear interpolation.
The composite uses time-stamped and National LIDAR Programme surveys and favours the newest best-resolution survey where coverage repeats.
The 1 metre DSM covers approximately 99 percent of England.
It uses last or only laser returns and includes vehicles, buildings, vegetation and the terrain surface.
It is available as GeoTIFF rasters in 5 kilometre tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
The 2 metre DSM covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The page states vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
The dataset exposes WMS, WCS, WMTS, metadata WMS/WFS and OGC API service routes.
The National LIDAR Programme coverage metadata uses EPSG:27700.
Full coverage metadata downloads are offered as File Geodatabase, GeoJSON, GeoPackage and Shapefile ZIP archives.
The dataset period runs from 11 November 2016 to 5 May 2023.
OS Terrain 5 is a detailed Great Britain DTM supplied as a grid of heighted points and contours at five metre intervals.
The product is updated quarterly in January, April, July and October.
The documentation describes a typical accuracy level better than 2 metres RMSE and provides free Exeter sample data in ASCII, shapefile and GML formats.
The product download page directs product acquisition through the OS Data Hub.
The OS Terrain XML product schema is provided through the Ordnance Survey XML resources.
Supporting resources are grouped for contour products, gridded products and viewing-style metadata.
The known-data-issues page records issues affecting OS Terrain 5.
Resolved issue details remain on the page until the next product release.
The page currently reports no live known data issues.
Grid height values are calculated at pixel centres.
Tile-average tidal heights can create a small discrete step between adjacent coastal tiles.
Contour data is represented by polyline and spot-height features, with INSPIRE-derived feature terminology.
Per-tile XML metadata follows the GEMINI standard used for the UK Location Programme and INSPIRE.
Metadata identifies the 5 kilometre tile, spatial representation, British National Grid and the elevation topic.
The Esri asc.aux.xml file supplies minimum, maximum, mean and standard-deviation height statistics to support consistent styling.
The national supply reports 10,579 grid tiles and 10,572 contour tiles.
The full Great Britain tiled dataset is downloadable through OS Data Hub or OS Orders.
The supply is refreshed quarterly; approximate compressed national sizes are 16 GB for grid, 2.6 GB for GML contours and 2.5 GB for shapefile contours.
